purpose: Improve execution speed by translating existing text-processing loops into native code while preserving every observable retrieval decision and source coordinate.
allowed_changes: Equivalent native implementations of existing pure text-processing functions
Backend selection, build, distribution and validation required to execute those implementations
frozen_semantics: Database schema, SQL, candidate limits, ranking, tie order and scope policy
Normalization order, Unicode code-point coordinates and exact source spans
Segmentation, stable identifiers, context budgets, result caches and public payloads
implementation_candidate: CPython C extension with the existing Python implementation retained as an explicit reference and portability fallback
implementation_rationale: Direct CPython Unicode access avoids converting existing strings to a second representation. Language choice is not itself a measured performance claim.

formal_requirements.result_cache: disabled; cache clearing outside the timed region
formal_requirements.timing_boundary: Native recall call or actual official-SDK stdio MCP tool roundtrip; no generation model
formal_requirements.quality_scope: Existing synthetic61 and public1015 datasets are performance and equivalence regressions, not independent evidence of retrieval superiority.
formal_requirements.equality: All complete per-query outputs, source spans and indexed/source contents must agree; exclude only latency_ms from semantic payload comparisons.
identity: all runtime Python and native source hashes
Python, SQLite, Unicode and dependency versions
formal_requirements.publication: Keep every completed round and failed gate. Publish measured effects per surface and cohort, including regressions; never infer end-to-end speed from microbenchmarks or operation counts.
formal_requirements.acceptance: Exact semantic equality and all release gates are mandatory. Native acceleration must demonstrate a repeatable improvement on the primary paired measurements without a material unexplained regression before becoming the default. Unsupported build targets keep the unchanged Python implementation.
